title: Air Traffic Controller-Trainee (Sgt to Pvt) BMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
6.     MOS 7251, Air Traffic Controller-Trainee (Sgt to Pvt) BMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. While undergoing instruction under general supervision,
trainees pursue qualifications in Air Traffic Control, MOS 7257.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess a GT score of 110 or higher.




                                           3-448                        Enclosure (1)
 3147                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



            (2) Security requirement:     Secret security clearance eligibility.

        (3) Must be a Cpl or below and have less than 5 years TIS if desiring
LATMOVE into MOS. This is based on MOS proficiency and qualification
timeline requirements.

        (4) Must meet the physical requirements of and pass a medical
examination per NAVMED P-117, chapter 15, article 95, before beginning Air
Traffic Control Basic Course (ACA1).

                (a) Phorias -NOHOSH.

                (b) Slit Lamp Examination-required for applicants.

                (c) Intraocular Pressure-must meet aviation standards.

                (d) Hearing applicants must meet SNA applicant standards.

                (e) Reading Aloud Test-The "Banana Oil" test is required for all
applicants.

            (f) Color vision-must meet Class I standards.         Must pass anyone
of the following two tests:

                1. FALANT or OPTEC 900: 9 of 9 correct on the first trial
or, if any are missed, at least 16 of 18 correct on the combined second and
third trials.

                2. PIP color plates (Any red-green screening test with at
least 14 diagnostic plates; see manufacturer instructions for scoring
information), randomly administered under Macbeth lamp: scoring plates 2-15,
at least 12 of 14 correct.

            (g) Visual acuity, distant and near-no limit uncorrected. Must
correct to 20/20 or better in each eye. If the Armed Forces Vision Test
(AFVT) or Goodlite letters are used, a score of 7/10 on the 20/20 line
constitutes meeting visual acuity requirements.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Air Traffic Control Basic Course (ACA1) (N2367A2),
NATTC, NAS Pensacola, FL.

        (2) Complete the Marine Air Traffic Control and Landing System
(MATCALS) Operator Course (N23E4A2).

    d. Duties. For a complete list of duties and tasks, refer to reference
(bo), Aviation Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Enlisted Military Training/Reporting/Special Duty Code (no related SOC) 00-
0001.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.




                                           3-449                        Enclosure (1)
 3147                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L
common_text: The Air Control, Air Traffic Control, Air Support, And Antiair Warfare OccFld includes the operation and management of the air command and control functions associated with the Marine Aircraft Wing. Qualifications required include manual dexterity for man-machine interface, highly developed visual/auditory skills, the ability to communicate effectively with radios, and the leadership and skills to work effectively as a member of a command and control team. The duties involve skills and procedures that are initially acquired through formal schools and further developed by individual and team training. Air Control, air traffic control, air support and antiair warfare Marines will be required to learn the emplacement, cabling orientation and operation of air command, control, traffic control, and antiair warfare defense systems and equipment. Entry- Level assignments include LAAD Gunner, Air Command and Control Operator, Air Traffic Controller, and Air Support Operations Operator. A wide variety of FMF billets are available in the OccFld in the active and reserve forces at group, squadron/battalion, or battery level. Numerous non-FMF assignments also exist at the Marine Corps Systems Command and Marine Corps Air Stations worldwide as instructors at MOS-producing schools. Marines will participate in routine air command and control functions while training for a designated MOS within the OccFld (see figure 3-38 for additional information concerning the career/grade structure and schooling of these Marines).

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
